claim: halinuxcompanion's author documents that the HA native (REST) API cannot reliably reflect a host going offline — if the app dies before sending the state, sensor values stick — and plans to move sensors to MQTT specifically because MQTT will-topics let the broker mark sensors unavailable when the client loses connectivity
stance_target: ha-linux-agent's MQTT architecture (with last-will/availability topics) is the correct design for the 'never reliable' offline-detection complaint; this is independent confirmation from an agent author who hit the native API's limits and chose MQTT
scope_conditions: halinuxcompanion project To-do; applies to native-app REST/websocket sensor reporting
quoted_support: Move sensors to MQTT — The reasoning for the change is the limitations of the API, naturally is expected that desktop and laptops would go offline and I would like for the sensors to reflect this new state. But if for some reason the application is unable to send this new state to Home Assistant the values of the sensors would be stuck. But if the app uses MQTT it can set will topics for the sensors to be updated when the client can't communicate with the server.

claim: halinuxcompanion receives actionable HA notifications by running a LOCAL aiohttp HTTP server that Home Assistant POSTs notification service calls to, with D-Bus used to display notifications and listen for action/clear events, plus D-Bus sleep/shutdown signals to update a Status sensor immediately before power events
stance_target: a third architecture pattern beyond push-vs-MQTT: HA calls INTO the agent over HTTP; requires the HA instance to reach every host on the fleet network — a constraint MQTT avoids (agent only needs outbound broker connectivity)
scope_conditions: halinuxcompanion on a LAN-reachable Linux desktop, port 8400 by default
quoted_support: HTTP Server (aiohttp): Listen to POST notification service call from Home Assistant ... Dbus interface (dbus_next): Sending notifications and listening to notification actions from the desktop, also listens to sleep, shutdown to update the status sensor

claim: halinuxcompanion registers as a mobile_app device in Home Assistant and exposes declarative notification-attached commands (suspend/poweroff/reboot/hibernate via systemctl, xdg-open, flatpak run) configured in config.json, run as a systemd --user service without sudo
stance_target: the mobile_app registration pattern plus declarative JSON command config is proven on Linux; but its narrow sensor set (cpu, memory, uptime, status, battery, camera_state) shows the native-API path yields fewer sensors than the MQTT agents
quoted_support: Now in your Home Assistant you will see a new device in the "mobile_app" integration, and there will be a new service to notify your Linux desktop. Notification actions work and the expected events will be fired in Home Assistant. ... "command_suspend": {"name": "Suspend", "command": ["systemctl", "suspend"]}
